info.description:
From gene names to annotations, gene coordinates and sequences.

- **search**: `/names` (prefix discovery), `/hits` (which annotations contain these exact gene names).
- **loci**: `/loci` (where those genes are: one row per gene, as json, tsv or ndjson).
- **downloads**: `/downloads` (queue a CDS, transcript or protein FASTA for up to 1,000 genes, poll it, fetch the gzipped file; `?dry_run=true` estimates), `/downloads/quota`, and `/transcripts` and `/genes/{locus_ref}/transcripts` (which transcripts a request would pick).
- **annotations**: per-annotation genes and cross-references (legacy shard-backed).
info.title: Annotrieve xrefs

post.description:
Queue a CDS, transcript or protein FASTA for the genes of a query or an explicit list.

All downloads wait in one queue (one runs at a time, because of the NCBI request budget). The
answer is `202` with the status; poll `GET /downloads/{id}` and fetch `/fasta` when `state`
is `done`. An equal request returns the download that exists.

parameters.description: only count and estimate; nothing is queued and no quota is used
parameters.name: dry_run

schema.description: only count and estimate; nothing is queued and no quota is used
schema.title: Dry Run

200.description: `dry_run=true`: the estimate. Otherwise the finished download already stored for an equal request (same body as GET /downloads/{id}).

202.description: Queued (or already queued/running for an equal request). `Location` is the status URL; poll it with `Retry-After`.

404.description: `no_genes_matched`, or a pinned/unknown locus (loci mode, on_error=fail)

413.description: `too_many_genes` or `too_many_sequences` (over the limit of one download)

429.description: `too_many_active_downloads` or `daily_quota_exceeded` for this client IP (see `Retry-After` and GET /downloads/quota)

503.description: `downloads_queue_full`, `downloads_capacity`, `annotations_unavailable`, `locus_ref_index_unavailable`, `plan_busy` (too many GFF-reading requests at once; see Retry-After)

get.description:
Presence search by exact gene symbol/synonym names.

``shape=compact``: ``terms``, ``fields``/``rows`` with ``matched`` (term indices).
``shape=records``: one object per annotation with ``n_matched``, ``n_terms``, ``missing`` and
``download_url``. Both carry ``facets`` (annotation counts per source, before the ``sources``
filter is applied).

The answer is never paged: it always lists every matching annotation (at most one row per
annotation, so about 18,000 rows or 9 MB in the worst case). A key named ``rows`` is a list of
arrays described by ``fields``; a key named ``results`` is a list of objects. ``shape`` in the
answer says which one you got.
